title: 5-Year Treasury Note auction (November new issue) — the belly leg of Thanksgiving week's three-day coupon block
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), RE-FETCHED direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 by this event's own initial research (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream — NOT carried from either proposing sweep's transcription. Row reads verbatim `5-Year NOTE Thursday, November 19, 2026 Tuesday, November 24, 2026 Monday, November 30, 2026` (announcement / auction / settlement) with NO trailing `R`, so a new issue — consistent with all 326 nominal 5-Year auctions on the fiscaldata record since 1995, none of which is a reopening. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. The same fetch shows the schedule's own holiday line `Holiday - Thursday, November 26, 2026`. STAYS ESTIMATE on the one limit that applies at D-76: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this sale is 71 days from its own announcement. The confirming primary is the 2026-11-19 announcement itself. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN BY THIS EVENT'S OWN INITIAL RESEARCH (2026-09-09), after reading BOTH prior proposals per docs/process/EVENT-RESEARCH.md: `proposals/treasury-5y-note-2026-11-24.from-treasury-2y-note-2026-11-23.json` and `proposals/treasury-5y-note-2026-11-24.from-treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-19.json` (both 2026-09-09). They agree on date, kind, impact and estimate status; this file adopts the 2Y sweep's title because it names the block. The one substantive disagreement they record — whether the 5Y deserves its own entry or belongs to its announcement — is settled the way the October block already was (treasury-5y-note-2026-10-27 and treasury-7y-note-2026-10-29 are canonical files), so November stays comparable with October. Both proposals stay where they are and are now shadowed. SIZE IS UNPUBLISHED TODAY and is not asserted here: `sb0590` (2026-08-05) read direct this session (HTTP 200) publishes an anticipated-size grid running `May-26 Jun-26 Jul-26 Aug-26 Sep-26 Oct-26` and STOPS — the 5-Year column reads 70 in all six rows, but there is no November row anywhere in the release. $70B is an EXPECTATION from 28 consecutive $70B prints (2024-04-24 -> 2026-08-26, fiscaldata, zero deviations) plus the release's verbatim guidance that Treasury 'anticipates maintaining nominal coupon and FRN auction sizes for at least the next several quarters'; the published figure arrives at the 2026-11-04 refunding. THE FINDING THAT EARNS THIS EVENT ITS LEDGER — the sibling treasury-5y-note-2026-10-27 ledger's headline curve effect is a REGIME property, not the par-curve mechanic it was read as. Extending that study out of sample (all 326 nominal 5Y auctions since 1995 against 7,176 par-curve sessions 1998-01-02 -> 2026-09-08, both pulled today): the 5Y-minus-avg(3Y,7Y) move on a 5Y auction day runs -1.69bp (t = -9.84) in 2023+ but only -0.21bp (t = -1.81) across 1998-2022 (n=247) — permutation p = 0.00001 on 100k draws, diff-in-diff -1.78bp now against -0.22bp then. A par-curve FITTING artifact cannot switch on in 2022-2023, because Treasury has fitted to on-the-runs throughout. Two further tests break the mechanical reading outright. (1) THE EFFECT REVERSES: 2023+ event time runs D+0 -1.69 (t=-9.8), D+1 +0.55 (t=+5.1), D+2 +0.29, D+3 +0.49, cumulating to +1.33bp over D+1..D+3 (t=+8.97, 40 of 43 positive) against +0.03bp on all 2023+ sessions — 79% of the dip is given back in three sessions, which is a concession round trip, not a re-anchoring. Pre-2023 D+1 is -0.47bp (t=-5.3), the opposite sign. (2) ONLY THE 10-YEAR IS STRUCTURAL: own-minus-neighbours on new issues, pre-2023 vs 2023+, reads 2Y -0.09 -> -4.29, 3Y +0.60 -> -3.10, 5Y -0.21 -> -1.69, 7Y +0.84 -> -1.09, but 10Y -1.65 (t=-6.0, n=92) -> -1.60 (t=-8.7, n=15), unchanged across 25 years; the 3Y and 7Y had the OPPOSITE sign before 2023. SECOND FINDING, A CLEAN NEGATIVE THAT CORROBORATES THE 2Y SIBLING AT A SECOND TENOR: Thanksgiving week is not a discount here either. Across the 14 in-week 5Y auctions since 1998 the relative move is -0.96 vs -0.41 out (p = 0.27) and the outright gap that looks marginal on the full sample (p = 0.056) is entirely 2008's -18bp — 2018+ reads in-week 0.00 vs out -0.09 (p = 0.98) with bid-to-cover 2.408 in-week vs 2.415 out. The two $70B-era Thanksgiving-week sales covered 2.43 (2024-11-26) and 2.41 (2025-11-25) against an era median of 2.360. THIRD — THE CROWDED SESSION DOES NOT DILUTE IT, which matters because 11-24 is the block's busiest supply day: the same schedule fetch puts a 2-Year FRN reopening, a 6-Week bill and a 52-Week bill on 11-24 alongside this sale, where 11-23 carries only the 2Y note and the 13/26-week bills. Measured, 2023+ 5Y auctions sharing their session with a 2Y FRN run -1.88bp on the relative measure against -1.33bp when the 5Y sells alone — the reverse of the n=5 dilution hint the 10-27 sibling flagged at the 2Y. Far from FOMC is likewise the STRONGER case (-2.00bp, t = -7.50, n=20, vs -1.41bp near), and 2026-11-24 is D-15 to fomc-2026-12-09.
